title: a shim's last_known berths under its rack folder, and the alias-named strays migrate home
intention: A shim keeps its last_known under the rack folder that declares it, so a device whose shim answers to a declared name (dbproxy as database, inferenceproxy as inference) writes no alias-named directory in instance-space, and the strays already standing migrate home once and are gone.
why: Measured 2026-11-20 on akiendelllinux: ~/.cairn/devices/database/0/ and ~/.cairn/devices/inference/0/ each hold only last_known.json, beside the real dbproxy/ and inferenceproxy/ dirs. BaseShim._last_known_path (cairn/tools/base/shim.py:1173) keys the file by device_id, and of the 11 rack shims exactly the two proxies have a device_id that differs from their folder (database vs dbproxy, inference vs inferenceproxy; measured by importing each shim class). The stray dir is what reddened bin/proofs/test_cairn_instance_address.py clause (b) (ticket 07d73ffa129c) and, before 8c5fdb750b75, broke `cairn inference`. 8c5fdb750b75's bounds.out names this verbatim: 'cairn/tools/base/shim.py (where a shim keeps last_known is its own ticket)'.
traces_to: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now) and Law 6 (one owner, one address)
how: BaseShim._last_known_path keys by the folder rack.folder_of(device_id) names when device_id is a charter's answers_as, else by device_id unchanged (the launcher's own rule, bin/cairn answers_as block). _read_last_known migrates: when the folder record is absent and the alias record stands, it reads the alias record, writes it under the folder atomically, removes the alias file and then the alias <n>/ and <alias>/ dirs if left empty; when both stand, it reads the folder record and removes the alias one. The red-first proof runs over a scratch instance root (address.ROOTS) with a throwaway shim whose device_id is a real charter's answers_as.

clauses.claim: a shim whose device_id is a charter's answers_as persists last_known at instance_path(<declaring folder>, n)/last_known.json, and nothing is created at instance_path(device_id, n)
a shim whose device_id is no charter's answers_as persists last_known at instance_path(device_id, n)/last_known.json, byte-path unchanged

migration: with last_known only at the old alias address, a fresh shim's cold read returns that record, the record then stands under the folder, and the alias file, its <n>/ dir and the alias dir are gone
with a record at both addresses, the cold read returns the folder's and the alias file is gone

no other caller of the last_known path breaks: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim.py, test_root_verbs.py, test_root_verb_vocabulary.py and bin/proofs/test_a_declared_name_outranks_a_stray_instance_dir.py pass unchanged

decisions.text: D1: BaseShim._last_known_path keys by rack.folder_of(device_id, repo root).name when device_id is a charter's answers_as, else device_id; the folder is resolved once per shim and cached.

D2: _read_last_known migrates: folder absent and alias present -> read alias, write folder atomically through _persist_last_known, unlink the alias file, rmdir the alias <n>/ and <alias>/ only if empty; both present -> read folder, unlink alias. Never rmtree.

D3: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over a scratch instance root (monkeypatch address.ROOTS as test_shim.py does) with a throwaway shim whose device_id is dbproxy's answers_as 'database'; tooth 5 runs the standing callers of the last_known path as subprocesses.
D4: bin/cairn's comment at the answers_as block stops saying the shim keeps last_known under its device_id; comment only, no code line changes.

out: the proxies' code and charters (device_id stays the bus name)
